families.notes: The word the whole Euthyphro argues about.
A contract verb. Behind English “poet” — one who makes.

words.notes: In Plato λόγος is usually “argument” or “account”, not simply “word”.
Stem supplied by hand: the corpus invariant stopped at θάλα-, which is not the standard analysis.
3rd declension: the stem is really χρηματ-, visible in the genitive χρήματος. The nominative hides the tau.
Comparative of νέος. The corpus invariant stopped inside the comparative suffix -τερ-, so the stem is supplied by hand.
Irregular: most forms use the stem μεγαλ-, as in μεγάλου.
Deponent: middle in form, active in meaning.
παρά (beside) prefixed to ἔχω — “hold out to”, hence “provide”.

passages.notes: The opening line of the dialogue. τί νεώτερον is literally “what newer thing?” — Greek uses a comparative where English would not.

passages.translation: Thucydides the Athenian wrote up the war of the Peloponnesians and the Athenians.
passages.notes: The first sentence of the Histories. Thucydides names himself in the third person — a convention of Greek historiography.
